I came back to Battlefield 2042 after playing Battlefield 6 and honestly I never expected to say this

I used to hate Battlefield 2042 I was one of the people who thought it was a huge disappointment. But after spending a lot of time with Battlefield 6 I decided to go back to 2042 and now I finally understand what this game was trying to be

For me, Battlefield 2042 is simply more comfortable and more fun to play.

The visual presentation might not be as technically impressive as Battlefield 6, but I actually prefer how 2042 looks and feels. The image is clear, the characters are easy to see, the UI is comfortable, and the menus are simple and easy to understand. I can look at my loadout, weapons, attachments and character and immediately know what I'm doing.

And the biggest thing for me is the sandbox.

The vehicles, jets and helicopters are a huge part of what makes Battlefield feel like Battlefield. I love being able to spend time learning how to fly, practicing maneuvers, attacking objectives and just having those crazy Battlefield moments that you remember after the match.

Battlefield 2042 also gives me that feeling of freedom that I personally miss in Battlefield 6.

Now, Battlefield 6 definitely has some great things. The graphics are impressive, the animations are polished, the gunplay can feel satisfying, and the overall presentation is very modern.

But after playing it for a long time, I started noticing things that really bothered me.

For me, the visual design is sometimes too busy, the weapon presentation doesn't feel as good, and the overall experience doesn't feel as comfortable to read and play as 2042. The game can look technically incredible while still not looking or feeling better to my eyes.

And that's the important part:

Technical quality doesn't automatically mean better gameplay.

I bought and played both games. I gave Battlefield 6 a real chance. And instead of making me forget about 2042, it actually made me appreciate 2042 more.

So yeah…

I went from:

I hate Battlefield 2042.

to:

Why the hell am I having more fun here than in Battlefield 6? 😂

I'm going back to 2042, and this time I'm actually going to learn the game properly — especially the jets and helicopters.

Maybe 2042 wasn't as bad as I thought.

Maybe I just needed Battlefield 6 to make me appreciate it.

Back to 2042. ✈️🚁🔥

[b]Playtime:[/b] 75 hours
[b]Genre:[/b] Multi-Billion Dollar Corporate Trash / Broken FPS Simulator
[b]Verdict:[/b] An absolute dumpster fire of a video game, a catastrophic insult to the entire franchise, and a pristine monument to EA's relentless mission to treat its player base like miserable cash cows begging to be milked dry.

[h1]1. The Technical Catastrophe & Linux Ban[/h1]

[b]The Unannounced Linux Theft:[/b] Out of absolute nowhere, EA dropped a predatory anti-cheat update that completely locked out and banned the entire Linux community without a single word of warning or a penny of compensation—effectively stealing a product people paid for overnight and ruining couples' co-op sessions across the globe.

[b]Day-One Bugs That Refuse to Die:[/b] Fundamental bugs that have plagued the game since its disastrous launch—such as the infamous camera glitch that forces your perspective straight underground the exact second you enter a vehicle, requiring a full game restart to fix—remain completely unpatched and ignored by lazy developers.

[b]The Broken Party System: Even if you are just trying to play a lonely solo match, the party system manages to glitch out, error-out, and boot you directly to the main menu, proving that basic, foundational multiplayer architecture is entirely beyond the capabilities of DICE.

[h1]2. Billions in Revenue, 15-Tick Server Garbage[/h1]

[b]Corporate Greed vs. Potato Servers: Electronic Arts pulls in billions of dollars in annual revenue and sits on massive corporate mountains of cash, yet they are quite literally too cheap, lazy, and incompetent to provide stable, decent server infrastructures. Back in the golden days of the franchise, we enjoyed crisp, responsive 60 Hz servers; today, we've regressed backward into a pathetic technological dark age with garbage servers sputtering down to a miserable 15 ticks. It is a staggering embarrassment to the industry.

[b]A Deserted Wasteland & Bot Fodder: The game is so completely dead and abandoned that you spend half your matches dumping entire magazines into braindead AI bots or jogging for ten minutes across massive, lifeless, empty maps under a poorly scripted sandstorm.

[b]Rigged Hitboxes & Catch-Up Mechanics: Tank shells phase right through enemy armor for zero damage, point-blank chest shots get swallowed by a broken netcode, and EA's notorious catch-up/rebound mechanics actively cheat behind the scenes to artificially manufacture fake, unearned momentum.

[h1]3. Tone-Deaf Specialists & The Apex Legends Clone[/h1]

[b]Wish.com Call of Duty: EA took our beloved military sandbox franchise, ripped its heart out, and handed us a bootleg Apex Legends clone packed with cringe-inducing specialist heroes dropping Marvel-tier quips while sliding around on skateboards across ruined, sterile battlefields.

[b]An Insult to the Community: Every single pixel of this software screams corporate contempt. The gunplay feels like a leaky garden hose, vehicle physics are coded by legally blind interns, and the overall visual aesthetic looks like a neon-soaked diarrhea burst under fluorescent lights.

[h1]4. The Bleak, Hopeless Outlook on Battlefield 6[/h1]

[b]Here We Go Again with BF6: When you look at what is currently brewing with Battlefield 6, it's the exact same nauseating corporate cycle all over again. Sure, we had the mandatory honeymoon marketing phase designed to lull us to sleep and empty our pockets, but the cash machine is already revving up, the old corporate demons are creeping right back in, and it's starting to rot into the exact same sanitized, lifeless garbage as 2042.

[b]Cancer vs. Explosive Gastro: Let's be completely, brutally honest: Battlefield 6 might be factuellement a tiny bit less vomit-inducing and marginally more playable than its chromosomal disaster of an older brother, but that's like comparing stage-4 cancer to a vicious, explosive bout of food poisoning—either way, you end up staring straight into the toilet bowl regretting every single life choice that brought you there. Flee this franchise like the plague, spit on EA's shareholders, and stop buying their lukewarm corporate soup.

So much potential, such a terrible landing.

Definitely better than initial release, although as a 'Battlefield' title it still falls short of overtaking Battlefield 1 or Battlefield V in terms of classic IP mechanics and styling; and the nerfs to character gadgets, movement and items that were considered 'meta' in past updates did little to keep a portion of players who stayed aboard for this 'signature' experience; when others refused to pay for entry.

Although, in a strange paradox, when I played it out of spite or with friends and treated it like a generic FPS instead of a Battlefield title, it actually was enjoyable. I sincerely believe that if this was launched as a standalone title by DICE instead of a series successor, it would have probably done better- but as a 'sequel', it falls (just) short.

Maybe in another life, if it had a smoother launch, had a less 'exotic' wrapper and a more grounded mechanical shift, it could have been a treasure to the lineup, instead of the awkward experiment in was discounted as.

Get it on sale, play it as a standalone non-successor and you might get a few good hours out of it like I did.
But as a full-price 'Battlefield'? I would hold on to your wallet until next time.
